A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AGSER for zero-shot hallucination detection. All 15 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments with four LLMs on Books, Movies and GCI, including pilot studies, ablations, sensitivity analyses and worked examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds intermediate-layer ablation results and three failure cases in Appendices G and I.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes the documented token-importance calculation: Equation 2 replaces attention-weighted value/output projections with a scalar sum of attention weights across heads. This revises one scoring component; Algorithm 1 retains the query split, answer regeneration, Rouge-L comparisons and final score.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Books, Movies and GCI factual-recall tasks. The added layer tests and failure cases remain within this coverage; newly disclosed dataset sizes do not establish a coverage change.

E2.justification: Table 3 evaluates the same four baselines: SBERT, SelfCheckGPT, INSIDE and InterrogateLLM. Baseline descriptions move to Appendix C, and newer related-work citations do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Tables 29–32 add intermediate-layer configurations, including Llama2-7b layers 8/24 and Qwen2.5-14b layers 8/16/32/40. The main AUC metric, model sizes, five baseline resamples, k = 2/3 and lambda = 1 remain unchanged. Dataset counts and all-test usage are newly disclosed rather than demonstrated protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Appendix G extends the existing layer-choice ablation to additional intermediate layers. Appendix I adds three failure cases examining omitted query information and consistently repeated incorrect facts. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter studies and successful examples are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly states that results use a single run with random seed 42. v1 does not report this information. Neither version provides confidence intervals or significance tests, and no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: The original main tables, pilot distributions and eight worked examples retain their values. v3 adds layer-specific AUCs, such as 0.744/0.857/0.996 for Llama3-8b layer 24 on Books/Movies/GCI, and failure-case consistency scores of 0.4, 0.99 and 0.24. These extend the reported results without changing default benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes the attention scaling denominator from sqrt(d_h/H) to sqrt(d_h). Equation 2 replaces the projected vector contribution with a scalar head sum, resolving the vector/scalar mismatch in the token-ranking definition. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: attention-guided self-reflection, effective zero-shot detection and reduced inference overhead across four LLMs and three benchmarks. Defining zero-shot explicitly and replacing 'complexity' with 'overhead' do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly explains AGSER failures through loss of essential query information and persistent incorrect model memories. Section 6.1 also explains the use of fixed, untuned hyperparameters through limited availability of model-specific validation labels. Existing access and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds dataset counts of 3000/3000/181 and all-test/no-training usage, discloses the absence of per-dataset hyperparameter tuning, and specifies A100 80GB hardware and SpaCy, transformers and rouge versions. Appendix E adds licensing information. Existing prompts and model-access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds six 2025 references by Chen, Cheng, Fang, Huo, Sun and Zhong, modestly extending discussion of graph-based consistency, decoding, alignment and internal representations. It also explains excluding supervised internal-state detectors from the zero-shot comparison. AGSER's overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v3 makes localized wording clarifications, moves baseline descriptions into Appendix C, reorganizes the retained appendices around new documentation and analyses, and updates author, affiliation and acknowledgment text.

P2.justification: v3 adds dataset-statistics Table 6 and four layer-ablation tables, compacts the appendix prompt displays and relocates Algorithm 1. The main illustration, sensitivity plots and principal result-table displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical clarity through a scalar token-score definition, supplies useful reproducibility details, and adds targeted layer checks and concrete failure analysis. These make the paper easier to assess and reproduce. The gains remain limited: principal results are unchanged, and the newly disclosed single-run evaluation still lacks uncertainty estimates.
